negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-registered core banking software product vendor was found. All core banking in ME appears to be supplied by foreign/regional vendors, with ME firms acting as integrators, front-end/CRM suppliers or channel operators.
negative_findings.result_summary: sr and en queries on 'implementacija core banking sistema Crna Gora integrator' and 'Montenegro core banking implementation references' returned only global vendor/consultancy marketing (Capgemini, Sopra, Temenos lists) and no ME-domiciled core banking supplier or ME-named implementation reference.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means the vendor-intelligence signal for core banking in ME must be harvested from bank-side disclosures and regional vendor sites (workstreams other than A6), not from ME corporate reference pages.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegro-based card production or card personalisation bureau identified.
negative_findings.result_summary: sr query 'personalizacija kartica Crna Gora kompanija' returned only Serbian bureaus (Cards Print, SIS Kartice, PVC-kartice, MHT) and generic tourism payment pages; no ME-registered personalisation provider surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests ME banks source card personalisation cross-border (most likely RS or HR bureaus). Personalisation vendor intelligence for ME therefore has to be collected from Serbian/regional bureau reference pages and from bank card-issuance tender documents.

negative_findings.description: No ME-local authorised distributor/service partner page found for ATM OEMs (NCR/NCR Atleos, Diebold Nixdorf, Hyosung, GRG).
negative_findings.result_summary: sr query mixing OEM names with 'distributer partner Crna Gora bankomati isporuka' returned only global ATM-industry press and parts marketplaces; no ME partner-locator entry surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Reinforces the picture that Payten is effectively the single ATM supply-and-service channel in ME. Should be re-tested directly against each OEM's partner-locator page rather than via search engines.

negative_findings.description: Logate's clients page is not at the guessed path.
negative_findings.result_summary: https://logate.com/clients/ returned HTTP 404. The equivalent content lives at https://logate.com/case-studies/ and https://logate.com/partners/, confirmed from the site's own navigation.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection configs must use the real /case-studies/ and /partners/ paths; treat the 404 as a path error, not evidence the vendor publishes no references.

negative_findings.description: Several ICT Cortex members plausibly relevant to this cell were not individually opened this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: POS4, Financial Solutions, Euro Unit, ZZI, Domen, Codeus, Codelab, OmniTech and VG Group were captured from the cluster directory but only partially or not characterised; their reference pages remain unread.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's candidate list is therefore a floor, not a ceiling; a second pass opening each cluster member's site would likely add several genuine vendor/reference sources.

negative_findings.description: The routine playbook file on disk could not be consulted.
negative_findings.result_summary: The stated playbook path (C:/Users/User/Dropbox/...) is a Windows path and this session runs on macOS; no equivalent local copy was located, so the method followed is the one embedded in the task prompt.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any playbook-specific classification conventions or field semantics not restated in the prompt may not be reflected in this slice.

coverage_gaps.description: Field-service and hardware-maintenance firms (ATM cash-handling, safes, CIT, terminal repair) in ME beyond Payten are essentially invisible in web search.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search sr terms 'servisiranje bankomata', 'transport novca', 'trezorska oprema', 'CIT Crna Gora' and cross-check bank annual reports and CRPS activity codes for outsourced-service suppliers.

coverage_gaps.description: No ME public-procurement channel was mined this run, yet state banks/institutions publish tenders naming winning IT vendors and contract values.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add the Montenegro e-procurement portal (CEJN / cejn.gov.me) and the Ministry of Finance tender archive as pointer sources and filter on ICT and payment-system CPV categories.

coverage_gaps.description: Montenegrin Cyrillic-script and ijekavian spelling variants were only lightly exercised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run key queries with Cyrillic forms and ijekavian variants (rjesenja/resenja, bankarski sistem, platni promet, informacioni sistem) to reach sources that latinica queries miss.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor employment and project signals (job ads, LinkedIn project posts, conference sponsor lists) were not systematically harvested, though they often name bank projects before marketing pages do.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add ME job boards (posao.me, zaposli.me) and the TechnoBank/regional banking-conference sponsor and speaker lists as recurring pointer sources.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor reference pages are undated, so wins cannot be time-ordered from the page alone.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair each vendor crawl with Wayback Machine snapshots to date the first appearance of each named bank reference.

brief: Montenegro's banking/payments supplier landscape is unusually concentrated: the Asseco/ASEE family (Payten for ATM/POS supply and field service, e-mon for e-banking channels) accounts for most of the country's payments infrastructure and, helpfully, publishes bank-named references - Payten's news feed and the emon24.net client list together map most of the eleven ME banks to specific products. Genuinely Montenegrin actors cluster in two layers: bank-adjacent software houses with published case studies (Logate with CX360/Connect, 2BI which is itself a CBCG-licensed payment institution, Cikom as the veteran systems integrator) and a merchant-side POS/fiscalisation tier (VG Group/Adeo, eFiskal, SEKAS, POS4). No ME-domiciled core banking product vendor and no ME card personalisation bureau were found, which pushes that intelligence to regional vendors and bank-side disclosures. The strongest pointer assets for maintaining this cell are the ICT Cortex member directory, the MFIC member profiles and the CBCG financial-service-provider registers, with ME bank e-banking notice pages serving as the best independent, dated confirmation of vendor switches.
